full_judgment:
This is an application under section 38 of the Companies Act, 1913 for rectification of the Share Register of the respondent No.1 namely, Eastern Industries (Bangladesh) Ltd. The respondent No.1 is a private limited company. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 are the founder Directors of the company. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 are full brothers and the petitioner is the son of the respondent No 3 and nephew of the respondent No. 2. Since inception respondent Nos. 2 and 3 were running the company as a family company. The petitioner was also with the company since 1960 and looking after the production and labour control as an enamel expert. The respondent No. 3 was holding 1300 shares of the company. On 10.4.86 the respondent No. 3 out of natural love and affection, gave away all his 1300 shares by way of oral gift (Heba) to his son namely, the present petitioner, in presence of the witnesses. Respondent No. 3 also had sworn an affidavit before the Notary Public on 10.4.86 confirming his oral gift in presence of two witnesses namely, Mrs. Gulbanoo Amirali and Mrs. Niamat Sherali. The petitioner as donee accepted the aforesaid gift in presence of the witnesses, On the same day i.e. on 10.4.86 when the gift was made, the petitioner paid the share transfer stamp of Tk.1950/- in respect of the transfer of 1300 shares on the instrument of transfer. The petitioner submitted a letter before the company with a copy of the affidavit and the instrument of transfer for recording his name in the share register of the company as new shareholder in respect of the 1300 shares of his father. The instrument of transfer of shares has also been witnessed by 3 witnesses. 

 8. In the background of the aforesaid facts and circumstance of the case Mr. Md. Aminul Huq, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits the petitioner is entitled to get his name registered in the register of the company in respect of the 1300 shares of his father. He submits that the petitioner is the son of the respondent No.3 and the oral gift was made by the father followed by an affidavit before the Notary Public. Not only that it was followed by an instrument of transfer of shares. The alleged gift was made on 10.4.86 and the alleged transfer of 400 shares to Mrs. Amir Banoo was made on 30.1.86. Mr. Aminul Huq submits that the donor is declaring that he has made the aforesaid gift and the donee has accepted the gift since the donor is the father of donee. There is no legal infirmity in making such an oral gift under Mohammedan Law. The respondent No. 2 has no locus standi to say that it is not a valid gift He is not aggrieved in any manner whatsoever by such a gift.Moreover, after making the aforesaid gift on l0th April, 1986, on the same day the respondent No. 3 informed the company about the above oral gift by a letter dated 10.4.86. He also requested the company to issue fresh certificates to Mr. Sherali Virjee by that letter annexing the instrument of transfer as well as copy of the affidavit of gift. The present petitioner also wrote to the respondent No. 2 on 18.6.86 about the transfer of the aforesaid shares. The affidavit in respect of the gift as well as the instrument of transfer duly stamped with an amount of Tk.1950/- were also annexed with that letter sent by the present petitioner. The respondent No. 2 being Managing Director gave a reply on 3.7.86 to Amirali Virjee with reference to his letter dated 10.4.86. In that letter the Managing Director did not raise any Objection nor he disclosed that in January. 1986 the 400 shares had been transferred by the respondent No. 3 to Mrs. Amir Banoo. The respondent No. 2 gave a reply on 3.7.86 to the letter to the present petitioner dated 18.6.86. In that letter also the respondent No. 2 did not mention anything about the alleged transfer of 400 shares in favour of Mrs. Amir Banoo in January. 1986. Nor he did state a single word that the company did not believe the transfer of shares by way of gift.
